body:
From about 130 BCE, a web of trade routes linked China, Central Asia, India, Persia and the Mediterranean. We call them the Silk Roads. Merchants carried silk, spices, paper and horses. They also carried things you cannot pack on a camel: religions, languages, technologies and diseases.

In this unit you will:
- trace the routes on a map and explain why oasis towns grew rich,
- explain how the Silk Roads spread ideas as well as goods,
- read a famous traveler's description of paper money and decide how far to trust it.

Key words: caravan, caravanserai, oasis, relay trade, cultural diffusion, missionary, currency.

Question to keep in mind: what travels farther, a bolt of silk or an idea?
title: More Than Silk
